And even if somehow you manage to make it robust against cheating which is possible theoretically, you still have the problem of matchmaking. Such a zero sum game survives on a constant influx of new players losing all the money they bet. After a while it becomes really evident that getting involved in such a game as a noob is a pure waste of money (a lot of money). This phenomenon already happens with games that don't have betting. I have never played CS in my life, I wouldn't want to install CS:GO and go through months of training before I become close to decent, it's just not worth it.

As to your second point, if that were the case (new players just show up and lose everything), no one new would ever learn to play poker.

Real gambling gets around this by having tables with different limits. Newer players go to low-limit tables where they can get a decent amount of entertainment without risking a huge bankroll, and thus are matched against other newer players. More experienced players go to higher-limit tables to increase their payout.

You do occasionally get a "shark" - an experienced player that goes to a low-limit table to clean house - but it's such a small payout in comparison to what they could make in the same amount of time at a higher limit table that it's generally not worth it.
